response.cue_rationale: “Uncle” also covers other relationships and address uses; “parent’s brother” makes the shared kinship sense explicit and fits both answers.

preference_risk.rationale: A formal Malaysian alternative exists, but it is not the usual everyday preference over “pak cik” for this cue.

response.rationale: “Paman” is the ordinary Indonesian term for a parent’s brother, while Malaysian Malay commonly uses “pak cik” for this kinship sense. The pairing teaches a useful national preference, although “pak cik” can also be used more broadly as a respectful address for an older man.
response.risk_rationale: “Pak cik” has broader respectful-address uses beyond the specified kinship sense.
response.shared_synonym_rationale: Malaysian Malay also has the formal term “bapa saudara,” but ordinary usage generally favors “pak cik” in this everyday context, so it does not undermine the contrast.
